units.text: INT. GOLD STANDARD PAWN - DAY
A narrow shop crammed floor to ceiling: guitars on hooks, a glass case of watches, power tools in rows, a stuffed marlin over the register.
A buzzer on the door.
Dusty light.
IGNATIUS KOWAL, 60s, owner, bald and bespectacled, sits behind the counter with a jeweler's loupe.
DETECTIVE NASRIN FARHADI, 40s, in a wrinkled blazer, leans on the glass case with a notebook.
At a rack of coats, MAUREEN PELL, 50s, a regular, sorts through winter jackets she has no intention of buying.
The buzzer sounds.
A YOUNG MAN, 20s, in a hooded sweatshirt, hurries in with a pillowcase.
He sees the detective and stops.
I'll come back.
units.name: YOUNG MAN

units.text: You'll stay. Everybody stays at Gold Standard.
units.name: IGNATIUS

units.text: The young man hesitates.
Ignatius lowers the loupe.
The detective does not move, but her eyes follow him.
That's Trey Mackenzie. His mother is Maureen's cousin.
units.name: IGNATIUS

units.text: Second cousin.
units.name: MAUREEN

units.text: I just want to pawn this.
units.name: TREY

units.text: What is it?
units.name: DETECTIVE FARHADI

units.text: A... lamp.
units.name: TREY

units.text: Put it on the counter, Trey.
units.name: IGNATIUS

units.text: Trey sets the pillowcase down.
Ignatius opens it, peers in, and sighs.
A radio on the shelf crackles.
All units, burglary on Delmar Street, possible suspect on foot, gray hoodie.
units.name: DISPATCH

units.text: Nobody speaks.
Trey's hand drifts toward the pillowcase.
Detective Farhadi closes her notebook.
Trey, how about we take a walk?
units.name: DETECTIVE FARHADI
